comments.note: MainContentViewModel.OnRefreshStateChanged fires a fire-and-forget RefreshCountAsync ((_ = RefreshCountAsync())). If the method throws, the exception is silently swallowed. Consider attaching a continuation that logs the exception, consistent with how other fire-and-forget tasks are handled elsewhere in the codebase.

LibraryFoldersView.axaml uses a bare TextBlock for each folder row (showing only Path). Consider including AddedUtc or a tooltip to give the user context, especially when two folders share a basename.

MainContentViewModel.ShowLibraryFolders fires LoadFoldersCommand on every open (fire-and-forget). For a large folder list this could cause a visible flicker if the collection is cleared and repopulated each time. A guard to skip reload when Folders is already populated (or a cache-invalidation flag) would improve responsiveness.

The parameterless constructor on MainContentViewModel (retained for backward compatibility) leaves CurrentPage at Default and CurrentChildViewModel null, which is correct. However the XML doc comment only says 'retained for backward compatibility with tests'; it does not mention that navigation commands are no-ops when LibraryFolders/RefreshIndex are null. A short note would prevent future surprises.

DI registration for LibraryFoldersView, RefreshIndexView, LibraryFoldersViewModel, and RefreshIndexViewModel is deferred to WP-017. Until that WP lands, invoking ShowLibraryFoldersCommand in a running app will cause ViewLocator to call App.Services.GetRequiredService(LibraryFoldersView) and throw an InvalidOperationException. This is an intentional design decision documented in the handoff notes and is expected to be resolved in WP-017.

MainContentView.axaml Refresh Index button binds to RefreshIndex.StartRefreshCommand (chained null-propagation at runtime). When the DI-wired MainContentViewModel is not yet active (parameterless constructor path), RefreshIndex is null and the binding silently no-ops — this is safe but untested.

Parameterless constructor doc comment improved to document the no-op navigation behaviour. Build: 0 warnings. 313/313 tests pass — no regressions.

comments.note: MainContentViewModel: added IDisposable implementation with Dispose() that unsubscribes _orchestrator.StateChanged -= OnRefreshStateChanged. The full constructor subscribes to StateChanged but the original code had no unsubscription path. Once WP-017 wires the full DI constructor, the orchestrator (a singleton) would hold a rooted reference to the view-model indefinitely. The fix is purely additive — no behavioural change to the current parameterless-constructor production path.

MainContentViewModel parameterless constructor doc comment updated to explicitly state: (1) navigation commands are no-ops because LibraryFolders/RefreshIndex are null, and (2) Dispose() is also a no-op in this path. Flags the gotcha noted by the Developer in implementation comments.
